pharmacy.title: At the Pharmacy
pharmacy.subtitle: Ask for medicine for a cold or a headache.
pharmacy.culture: In China, most pharmacies sell over-the-counter medicine without a prescription, but antibiotics usually require a doctor's prescription. Pharmacists often ask whether you have a fever or an allergy before recommending anything.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ gǎn mào le.
dialogue.en: Hello, I have a cold.

dialogue.speaker: pharmacist
dialogue.en: Do you have a fever?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: A little.

dialogue.speaker: pharmacist
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè ge yào yī tiān chī sān cì.
dialogue.en: Take this medicine three times a day.

choices.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi gǎn mào yào.
choices.en: I want to buy cold medicine.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.pinyin: Zhè ge yào duō shǎo qián?
choices.en: How much is this medicine?
I need some fever medicine.

hospital-register.title: Registering at the Hospital
hospital-register.subtitle: Sign up to see a doctor and choose a department.
hospital-register.culture: In China, you must register (挂号) before seeing a doctor. Bring your ID and insurance card (医保卡), choose a department, and many people book online in advance to avoid long queues.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Hello, I need to register.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: receptionist
dialogue.en: Which department should I register for?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: I have a headache. Which department should I register for?

dialogue.speaker: receptionist
dialogue.text: 神经内科，今天上午还有号。
dialogue.pinyin: Shénjīng nèikē, jīntiān shàngwǔ hái yǒu hào.
dialogue.en: Neurology. There are still appointments available for this morning.

choices.en: I have a medical insurance card.
How much is the registration fee?
Can I register in the afternoon?

doctor-visit.title: Seeing the Doctor
doctor-visit.subtitle: Describe your symptoms clearly.
doctor-visit.culture: Chinese doctors often ask how long the symptoms have lasted and about your appetite and sleep. Being specific about when it started helps, and they may order a blood test first.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Doctor, I have a headache and a cough.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.en: How long has it been?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Liǎng sān tiān le, wǎnshàng gèng lìhai.
dialogue.en: For two or three days. It's worse at night.

dialogue.speaker: doctor
dialogue.en: Let's take your temperature first.

choices.en: I have a fever.
I don't want to eat.
Do I need a blood test?

dental.title: At the Dentist
dental.subtitle: Say which tooth hurts and ask about treatment.
dental.culture: Dental care in China is cheaper than in many Western countries, but medical insurance (医保) usually covers only basic treatment. A root canal or cleaning often starts with an X-ray.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Doctor, my tooth hurts.

dialogue.speaker: dentist
dialogue.en: Which tooth?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: This one, it hurts more at night.

dialogue.speaker: dentist
dialogue.en: You might need a root canal.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.en: Can I get pain relief first?
Is tooth extraction painful?
How much does it cost to get a tooth filled?

emergency.title: Calling an Ambulance
emergency.subtitle: Call 120 and give your address.
emergency.culture: To call an ambulance in China, dial 120. Give your exact address and stay on the line. Emergency rooms (急诊) at major hospitals are open 24 hours.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Hello, ambulance! Someone has fainted.

dialogue.speaker: operator
dialogue.en: Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒmen zài yángguāng xiǎoqū sān dòng.
dialogue.en: We're at Building 3, Yangguang Community.

dialogue.speaker: operator
dialogue.pinyin: Bié yídòng tā, wǒmen mǎshàng dào.
dialogue.en: Don't move him, we're on our way.

choices.text: 地址是解放路二十五号。
choices.en: The address is 25 Jiefang Road.
He's still breathing.
Please come quickly.

optician.title: Getting Glasses
optician.subtitle: Ask for an eye test and new glasses.
optician.culture: Glasses in China are affordable and made quickly, often within a day. The eye test (验光) is usually free when you buy frames and lenses, and optical shops are common in shopping malls.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng pèi yǎnjìng.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'd like to get glasses.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.en: Let's do an eye exam first.

words.en: particle indicating suggestion or softening tone

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Does the eye exam cost money?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Bú yào, xuǎn hǎo jìng kuàng zài suàn.
dialogue.en: No, it doesn't. We'll calculate after you choose the frames.

choices.pinyin: Pèi yī fù yǎn jìng duō shǎo qián?
choices.en: How much is it to get a pair of glasses?

choices.pinyin: Néng pèi yǐn xíng yǎn jìng ma?
choices.en: Can I get contact lenses here?
How long before I can pick them up?

massage.title: At a Massage or Foot Spa
massage.subtitle: Ask the price and book a session.
massage.culture: Foot massage (足疗) is a popular and affordable pastime in China, often 50 to 150 yuan for an hour. Many places offer private rooms, and tipping is not expected.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, zú liáo duō shǎo qián?
dialogue.en: Hello, how much is a foot massage?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Liù shí fēn zhōng bā shí kuài.
dialogue.en: It's eighty yuan for sixty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Can I soak my feet here?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Bāo kuò pào jiǎo, xiān huàn xié.
dialogue.en: It includes foot soaking. Please change into slippers first.

choices.en: Are there any openings available?

choices.pinyin: Àn mó jiān jǐng duō shǎo qián?
choices.en: How much is a shoulder and neck massage?
Can I get a receipt?

gym-signup.title: Joining a Gym
gym-signup.subtitle: Ask about membership cards and prices.
gym-signup.culture: Gym memberships in China are usually sold as monthly or annual cards, and the annual card is better value. Many offer a free trial, and personal trainers (私教) are sold separately.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, bàn yuèkǎ duōshǎo qián?
dialogue.en: Hello, how much is a monthly pass?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.en: A monthly pass is 300, and an annual pass is 1,800.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Do you have personal trainers?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu, xiān miǎnfèi tǐyàn yī cì.
dialogue.en: Yes, you can have a free trial first.

choices.en: Can I get a refund for the annual pass?
What time does the gym close?
Does it include access to the swimming pool?

blood-test.title: Getting a Blood Test
blood-test.subtitle: Ask about fasting and when results are ready.
blood-test.culture: For a blood test (抽血) in China, you usually need to fast for 8 to 12 hours beforehand. Results are often ready the same afternoon and can be viewed on the hospital app.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, yīshēng ràng wǒ yànxiě.
dialogue.en: Hello, the doctor asked me to get a blood test.

dialogue.speaker: nurse
dialogue.en: Have you fasted?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Yes, how many vials of blood will be drawn?

dialogue.speaker: nurse
dialogue.en: Two vials, and the results will be ready in the afternoon.

choices.en: Does it hurt?
How long do I have to wait?

choices.en: Can I eat now?

health-appointment.title: Booking a Check-up
health-appointment.subtitle: Make an appointment for a physical exam or follow-up.
health-appointment.culture: Physical exams (体检) are common in China and are often required by employers. Book ahead, arrive fasting in the morning, and bring your ID; results are usually ready within a few days.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng yùyuē tǐjiǎn.
dialogue.en: Hello, I would like to make a physical examination appointment.

dialogue.speaker: receptionist
dialogue.en: Which day would you like to book?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.en: Is this Friday okay?

dialogue.speaker: receptionist
dialogue.en: Yes, come on an empty stomach in the morning.

choices.en: How much is the physical examination?
What do I need to bring?
